messages.author: 10ee55c618d3a4c1
messages.subject: Cropping of axis labels
parts:
Hi all,

When I manually assign labels to an axis scale, long strings are cropped
at the edge of the plot area and thus only partially visible:

----
d <- data.frame(x=c(1:4), y=(1:4),
labels=c('Dear Hadley', 'could you fix this', 'before Christmas,',
'pretty pretty please with lots of cropping on top?'))

ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=d$x, labels=d$labels) +
opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(size=12, angle=-35, hjust=0))
----

I was able to work around this by adjusting plot.margin via opts(),
which works but is a bit tedious. So I thought I'd flag this in case
it's a bug or, if it is not, to ask whether there is a better way of
dealing with the problem.

Thanks,
Christian

messages.subject: Re: Cropping of axis labels
parts:
On Wed, Dec 22, 2010 at 4:48 AM, Christian Kreibich <chri...@icir.org> wrote:
Hi all,

When I manually assign labels to an axis scale, long strings are cropped
at the edge of the plot area and thus only partially visible:

----
d <- data.frame(x=c(1:4), y=(1:4),
               labels=c('Dear Hadley', 'could you fix this', 'before Christmas,',
                 'pretty pretty please with lots of cropping on top?'))

ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
 scale_x_continuous(breaks=d$x, labels=d$labels) +
 opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(size=12, angle=-35, hjust=0))
----

I was able to work around this by adjusting plot.margin via opts(),
which works but is a bit tedious. So I thought I'd flag this in case
it's a bug or, if it is not, to ask whether there is a better way of
dealing with the problem.

(a) Use a 90 degree angle - that would avoid the cropping problem (at least to the right).
(b) Use a less severe angle.
(c) Rotate the graph axis so that someone can more easily read the labels.
(d) Put line breaks in your labels to avoid overly long strings.
(e) Reduce the size of the text font.
etc.

Long labels are almost always better placed on the y-axis rather than the x-axis.

My opinion is this is a graphics design issue which doesn't require a software rewrite to solve. In my experience, if you need to insert long lines to annotate a graphic, you need to rethink how to construct your graphic. The more graphics space one assigns to the margins, the less area one has available for the actual graphic (not to mention the impact on the aspect ratio). If this is meant to go inside a document, you can use the caption for annotation or provide additional explanation in the text. For example, I almost never put titles on graphs that go in documents any more; I use the caption for that purpose.

Just my 2 pfennig.

Dennis

Thanks,
Christian
